target: megasporangiate strobilus (PO_0005032)
reason: Narrower: the paraphrase the treatments of Taxaceae and Cephalotaxaceae use for the reduced ovulate cone ('seed-bearing structures solitary, axillary'). PO_0005032 already lists ovulate cone and female cone as synonyms.

target: laminal cell (FLOPO_0986100) with position median (FLOPO_0991381) in the phyllid, pattern 18
reason: Moss descriptions: these are the laminal cells in the middle of the leaf, so a position of an existing class (fusiform, rhombic, 60-120 µm). No new class is needed.
'3-5-foliolées' is a count of leaflets stated as a quality of the leaf (pattern 03, compound word). 'foliolate' was already rejected as not a structure.

target: lamina (PO_0025060) part_of banner petal (PO_0025324), pattern 12
reason: The limb is the expanded blade of the papilionoid standard, above the claw. Standard is a synonym of banner petal, and the blade is its lamina.

target: achene fruit (PO_0030107) as the bearer, with rib as the counted part (flora_counted_parts: ribbed/costate → rib), pattern 03
reason: 'Rib' alone was rejected because it needs an organ, and here the organ is given. '8-12 ribs' is a count of ribs on the achene, like '8-12-ribbed', and 'ribs prominent' is a quality of that count. No rib class is needed.

target: lamina (PO_0025060) part_of lower petal (FLOPO_0996024, narrow synonym labellum), pattern 12
reason: There is no labellum class. The labellum is a narrow synonym of the positioned part 'lower petal', and its blade is the lamina of that petal. Shape, margin and size go on the lamina.

target: pinna (FLOPO_0985027)
reason: Narrower: the first-order divisions of a bipinnate leaf are its pinnae ('4-5 pairs of primary pinnae'). The leaflets of the next order are pinnules or leaflets.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of trichome (PO_0000282, the contextual sense of 'scale' for indumentum and rhizome scales), pattern 12
reason: The examples (cell lumina colourless, cells translucent and small) describe the cells of fern or lepidote scales. Those scales are trichome-like outgrowths under the existing sense rule for 'scale'. The rule applies only when the scale context is indumentum, not a bud or cone scale.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part_of staminode (PO_0009077), pattern 12
reason: A region (the apex) of an existing class.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020, synonym vein) part_of leaflet lamina (FLOPO_0986002); counts per side of the midrib follow pattern 14
reason: PO leaf lamina vein is a part of the leaf lamina. For leaflets the vein is a vascular bundle of the FLOPO leaflet lamina. '7-16 veins on each side of the midrib' is a count at a position.

target: style head (FLOPO_0986079)
reason: Narrower: in Proteaceae the pollen-presenter is the swollen top of the style that holds the pollen ('geniculate at junction with style', cylindric, 7-10 mm long). That is a style head used for secondary pollen presentation.
'Scale' already has several senses, and 'dorsal' gives only a position. The examples (fimbriate, filiform, absent in all material) do not name the organ, the family or the scale's sense.

target: second order inflorescence axis (PO_0006321)
reason: Narrower: the stalk of a partial inflorescence in a compound cyme or umbel is a first-order inflorescence branch. PO_0006321 has the synonym primary inflorescence branch. Peduncle (PO_0009053) is the stalk of the whole inflorescence.
A pyramidal pileus 5-20 mm high and 15-35 mm across is the cap of a fungus, such as stinkhorns in some African floras. It is outside the Plant Ontology and FLOPO's scope.

A generic part without its organ, like 'dorsal wing' and 'dorsal groove' before. These are probably mericarp ribs of Apiaceae ('1-3 of the dorsal ribs winged'), but the organ is not stated. With the organ, the count follows the counted part 'rib' (pattern 03).

target: corolline corona (FLOPO_0985021)
reason: Narrower: the pairs of linear or laciniate scales on the claw of the petal (Silene and Lychnis, and Sapindaceae) are corona outgrowths of the corolla. A count such as 'bearing 2 scales' is per petal (pattern 03).

target: tertiary leaf vein (PO_0008021)
reason: Narrower, collective: 'veinlet' is a synonym of tertiary leaf vein. The network ('lax', 'prominulous', 'plane or slightly impressed above') is described through its veins.

'Lobule' was rejected on 2026-11-13 as a generic part. Here it is evidently the small ventral lobe of a folded liverwort leaf (Lejeuneaceae, Frullania). That needs a liverwort leaf-lobule class first, which would be a separate proposal. The apex cannot be grounded before then.
These are perhaps the peltate sterile heads of cycad sporophylls (hexagonal, protuberant). The phrase does not name the organ, and 'sterile' was rejected as a part word.
A 'per X' fragment that names the container of a count ('strobili 1-2 per crown'), like 'per caudex' and 'per spathe' before. The counted part is the bearer.

target: phyllome sinus (PO_0025383) part_of corolla (PO_0009059), pattern 12
reason: PO defines phyllome sinus as the embayment between the marginal projections, typically lobes, of a phyllome. The sinus between corolla lobes is one of these, within the corolla.

target: laminal cell (FLOPO_0986100) at the base of the phyllid with position inner (FLOPO_0991378), patterns 12 and 18
reason: In moss descriptions these are the basal laminal cells away from the margin, as opposed to marginal or alar cells. They are elongate, porose, yellow and 20-30 µm long, so this is a position of an existing class.

target: bundle sheath extension (PO_0006022)
reason: Narrower: in grass leaf anatomy a girder is a sclerenchymatous strip that runs from the vascular bundle to the epidermis. PO defines bundle sheath extension as exactly this kind of strip, of parenchyma or sclerenchyma. 'Adaxial' and 'abaxial' are positions (pattern 18).
A 'per X' fragment giving the container of a count ('rosettes 1-5 per colony'). A colony is a group of plants, not a part.

target: branch (PO_0025073)
reason: Narrower: caudex is a synonym of stem, and a caudex branch is a branch of the stem near ground level (short, stout, elongate, absent).
A ratio of two dimensions of the bearer (pattern 11), like the rejected 'times as long as wide'.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part_of spathe limb (FLOPO_0986048), pattern 12
reason: A region (the apex) of an existing FLOPO class (acuminate, acute, cuspidate, caudate).

word: secondary veins on each side of midvein
target: secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140), counted per side of leaf midvein (PO_0020139), pattern 14 (count at a position)
reason: The phrase joins the counted part to its position. The position phrase alone ('on each side of midvein') was already treated as count_per_position for secondary leaf vein.
A position fragment of a count ('sori 4-8 on each segment'), like 'on each side' and 'per pinna'. The counted part (sorus, PO_0025359) is the bearer.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part_of paraphysis (PO_0030070), pattern 12; 'with/without a head' is better read as capitate or not of the paraphysis
reason: PO defines a paraphysis as a uniseriate trichome among the gametangia of bryophytes and pteridophytes. Its 'head' is the enlarged terminal cell or cells, a region of an existing class. 'Head obconic' is the shape of that apex.
